name: Week 10 APT29 and infostealer project evidence
description: Selected APT29/SolarWinds and StellarParticle CTI, checked against ATT&CK v20.1. Colors describe project evidence, not actor confidence or detection coverage. T1059.004 is excluded: the Linux lab is not evidence of APT29 use.

techniques.comment: Trojanized Orion software updates delivered SUNBURST. Delivery-chain context; not executed. Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor
PowerShell supported post-compromise commands and task operations. Weeks 5-7 contain the historical Windows PowerShell observations. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/
cmd.exe executed commands on remote machines. Historical cmd control is not validation of remote execution. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/

Existing scheduled tasks were temporarily modified, then restored. In the Week 8 Windows run c5dff010b214, the loader registered a new task with a logon trigger (Security 4698, record 507). It requested a manual start with schtasks.exe /run (4688, record 508). The marker action (4688, record 509) wrote the run ID. The loader then deleted the task (4699, record 524). Execution at a subsequent logon, modification and restoration of an existing task, and privilege escalation remain untested. Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor

RDP Bitmap Cache reconstruction showed a Chrome export of saved passwords to plaintext CSV (CrowdStrike figure 4). Mock JSON is not a browser credential store or DPAPI validation. Source: https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/observations-from-the-stellarparticle-campaign/

Shellbags showed Chrome and DPAPI directory navigation. Falcon identified the Cookie Editor extension used in the reported session reuse (figures 2–3). Fake cookies were archived; no valid session or cookie theft was tested. Source: https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/observations-from-the-stellarparticle-campaign/

Volexity recorded a 7-Zip command naming the exported local file C:\Temp\b.pst as its input on the OWA server. The lab has synthetic file opens and archive member checks. The reported Exchange collection is CTI only. Source: https://www.volexity.com/blog/2020/12/14/dark-halo-leverages-solarwinds-compromise-to-breach-organizations/

7-Zip created password-protected archives, sometimes split into parts. Week 9 exercised Linux tar/gzip and Windows tar.exe on synthetic files. Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2021/01/20/deep-dive-into-the-solorigate-second-stage-activation-from-sunburst-to-teardrop-and-raindrop/
Archives were staged on a victim OWA server. Local out/ artifacts do not demonstrate remote staging. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/

MITRE C0024 maps retrieval of a staged OWA archive over HTTPS to T1048.002. Volexity shows the 7-Zip command that created Redir.png and gives an illustrative HTTPS URL. The lab collected local archive telemetry. Volexity publishes no request log for the illustrated URL. MITRE: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/ Volexity: https://www.volexity.com/blog/2020/12/14/dark-halo-leverages-solarwinds-compromise-to-breach-organizations/
